newsitem.title: USA: CBOT rice ends up on export talk, heavy volume.
newsitem.headline: CBOT rice ends up on export talk, heavy volume.

text.p: CBOT rice futures closed higher on talk that Iraq may have bought rice from the U.S. and on prospects for another strong rice export number in Thursday's USDA weekly export sales report, traders said.
"It was mostly commercial buying and small spec buying. LIT (LIT America) bought the low and rallied it," a trader said.

Traders speculated the demand by LIT was cash-connected and may have been tied to a sale of rice to Iraq. Iraq was in the market this week for 30,000 tonnes of U.S. rice and Colombia was said tendering for 50,000 tonnes of rice.
Export sources said it was not likely that Iraq bought any rice from the U.S. but export action continues to drive the market.
"If the rice number is 70,000 to 80,000 tonnes tomorrow morning the game is back on," a trader said.

USDA early Thursday will release its weekly export sales report. The rice export tally has been running at a strong level in recent weeks and CBOT rice futures recently set a series of contract highs.
Rice closed seven to 12 cents per cwt higher, with March up 12 at $12.00-1/2 cent per cwt.
But the market collapsed its 30 cent per cwt trading limit Tuesday which put into effect the expanded 45 cent per cwt limits Wednesday and again Thursday.
Rice futures volume was estimated at a very strong 2,800 contracts, above the 1,086 traded Tuesday and above the record volume day of 2,215 traded June 12, 1995.
"It probably was the largest change of hands we've ever had down here," a trader said.
Traders also said there was huge spread action with 200 lots of March/July traded and 150 lots of March/May.
